title: Adding node 31
description: A 30-node key-value store places keys with hash(key) mod 30. A rehearsal for adding node 31 moves almost the whole dataset and overwhelms the network. Which placement scheme lets future growth move roughly a proportional share while spreading the transfer work across peers?

options.text: Use a faster hash function but continue taking the result modulo the node count.
options.explanation: Hash speed does not change the remapping caused by changing the modulus from 30 to 31.

options.text: Copy all data to node 31, then switch the client routing table.
options.explanation: That still moves the whole dataset and makes the new node a bottleneck rather than adding balanced capacity.

options.text: Increase the replication factor and keep modulo-based ownership.
options.explanation: More replicas may help availability, but ownership still reshuffles when the node count changes and more data must be transferred.

options.text: Use a consistent-hashing ring with many virtual nodes per physical node and throttle range transfers.
options.explanation: A joining node takes small token ranges from multiple peers, moving roughly 1/31 of ownership rather than nearly everything. Virtual nodes improve balance; zone-aware replica placement still matters.
